1. The Sun is larger than the average star (which are red dwarfs with radii of about 0.2-0.3 solar radii).
2. The Sun's size relative to an average star is several times larger, but not enormous by any standard definition.
3. The Sun would not be extremely bright compared to an average star.
4. The Sun would not be very dim compared to the smallest stars (red dwarfs), as it is actually brighter.

The best description is that the Sun would be enormous next to an average star.
